record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: For a normal translationally invariant matrix product state (MPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index, meaning the smallest scale at which the associated tensor becomes injective?

evidence.quote: Question 3 Which is the optimal upper bound for the injectivity index of a normal MPS in terms of its bond dimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $d\ge 2$ and $D\ge 1$. A translationally invariant matrix product state (MPS) on $n$ sites with physical dimension $d$ and bond dimension $D$ is determined by a tensor $A\in\mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D\times D}$, regarded as a tuple $(A_1,\dots,A_d)$ of $D\times D$ matrices. For each integer $L\ge 1$, define the linear map
$$\Gamma_L(A):\mathbb{C}^{D\times D}\longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes L},\qquad X\mapsto \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_L=1}^{d}\operatorname{tr}\!\bigl(X\,A_{i_1}A_{i_2}\cdots A_{i_L}\bigr)\,|i_1\cdots i_L\rangle.$$
Equivalently, $\Gamma_L(A)$ is injective iff the family $\{A_{i_1}\cdots A_{i_L}\}_{i_1,\dots,i_L}$ spans the full matrix algebra $M_D(\mathbb{C})$.

The tensor $A$ is called normal if there exists some finite $L$ for which $\Gamma_L(A)$ is injective. For a normal tensor $A$, its injectivity index is
$$\iota(A)\;=\;\min\{\,L\ge 1\,:\,\Gamma_L(A)\text{ is injective}\,\}.$$

Problem. Determine the exact best possible upper bound, as a function of the bond dimension $D$ alone, for the injectivity index of a normal translationally invariant MPS. That is, find the smallest function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\iota(A)\;\le\;f(D)$$
holds for every normal tensor $A$ with bond dimension $D$ (over all physical dimensions $d$), and exhibit normal tensors achieving (or asymptotically achieving) this bound.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of the optimal upper bound on the injectivity index of a normal MPS is closely tied to the quantum Wielandt inequality, where the best known general upper bound is on the order of $D^2\log D$ (Sanz–Pérez-García–Wolf–Cirac), while the best known lower-bound examples scale as $\Theta(D^2)$. Recent work has produced a "generic" quantum Wielandt inequality showing improved bounds for almost-all tensors, but the exact optimal worst-case bound in terms of $D$ alone remains unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Wielandt's inequality (Sanz, Pérez-García, Wolf, Cirac)
status_evidence.snippet: An upper bound to the number of times a channel must be applied so that it maps any density operator to one with full rank... the question about optimal bounds is left open.
status_evidence.claim: Best general upper bound is roughly D^2 log D; optimal bound left open.

status_evidence.title: A generic quantum Wielandt's inequality (Quantum, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Generic quantum Wielandt's inequality giving improved bounds for generic tensors and implications for MPS injectivity.
status_evidence.claim: Generic improvements exist but the worst-case optimal bound remains open.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical open problems in projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Lists determining the optimal upper bound for the injectivity index of a normal MPS in terms of bond dimension as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed among open problems on PEPS/MPS.
